entities.summary: Qantas Flight 32 was a regularly scheduled passenger flight from London to Sydney via Singapore. On 4 November 2010, the Airbus A380-800 operating the route suffered an uncontained failure in one of its four Rolls-Royce Trent 900 engines. The failure occurred over the Riau Islands, Indonesia, four minutes after takeoff from Singapore Changi Airport. After holding for almost two hours to assess the situation, the aircraft made a successful emergency landing at Changi. No injuries occurred to the passengers, crew, or people on the ground, despite debris from the aircraft falling onto houses in Batam.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Qantas Flight 32 incident led to a significant overhaul of engine safety regulations in Australia and globally, with the Australian Transport Safety Bureau (ATSB) conducting a comprehensive review of engine failure risks. The incident also highlighted the importance of crew training and emergency preparedness.
